title: Right derived functor of an exact functor
statement:
Let $F\colon\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be as in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] and moreover
exact. Then there is a canonical isomorphism $RF\cong D(F)$, where $D(F)\colon
D(\mathcal C)\to D(\mathcal D)$ is the functor induced by applying $F$ termwise.

proof.text:
An exact functor preserves cohomology, hence quasi-isomorphisms, so $D(F)$ is defined and
$Q\circ F\cong D(F)\circ Q$. A functor that already inverts the quasi-isomorphisms is its
own derived functor: $D(F)$ with this isomorphism as unit satisfies the universal property
of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Right derived functors are unique up to unique
isomorphism compatible with the units, which gives $RF\cong D(F)$.

lean.note: Comparison for the recorded dependency rightDerivedFunctorOfQuasiIsoResolutions, under exactly its arbitrary-quasi-isomorphism resolution hypothesis. The upstream rightDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory concerns a different chosen functor and requires HasKInjectiveResolutions (monomorphic resolutions), so cannot directly serve this interface. Reuses the dependency universal pair and uniqueness theorem and Mathlib mapDerivedCategory; the isomorphism is chosen from its unique unit-compatible characterization.
